name: Sustained 700 C (pottery kiln)
note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS. Updraught pottery kiln, wood fired. Free starting capability. Glazes, bricks, lime, glass working.

name: Sustained 1100 C (hand-blown charcoal)
note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS. Bloomery iron, bronze casting, glass melting. A man on a bellows tops out near here. Everything above this rung needs a machine.

name: Sustained 1300 C (water-blown continuous blast)
note: Liquid cast iron lives here. The jump from 1100 to 1300 is not more fuel, it is more AIR, continuously. This single rung is the difference between a bloomery civilisation and a foundry civilisation.

name: Sustained 1600 C (regenerative preheat)
note: Siemens regenerative preheat recycles flue heat into the incoming air. Crucible steel, open hearth, porcelain. You cannot get here by burning more charcoal; you must recycle the heat you are already throwing away.

name: 2000 C localised (oxy-hydrogen blowpipe)
note: A flame, not a furnace: small volume only. Fused quartz working, platinum melting, lime light.

name: 3000 C+ (electric arc / resistance)
note: No chemical flame reaches here. Calcium carbide, ferroalloys, tungsten, artificial graphite, synthetic corundum.

name: Tolerance 1 mm (skilled hand craft)
note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS, and is very good at it. Carpentry, masonry, bronze casting, the Antikythera gearwork. Free.

name: Tolerance 0.1 mm (file, scraper, gauge)
note: Needs a reference plane to scrape against and a gauge to check with. Clock wheels, lock work, decent screw threads.

name: Tolerance 0.01 mm (slide rest, lead screw, micrometer)
note: Take the tool out of the operator's hand and accuracy stops depending on his wrist. Steam pistons, interchangeable parts, precision instruments.

name: Tolerance 1 micron (lapping, grinding, optical flats)
note: Lapping with loose abrasive plus interference fringes to check. Gauge blocks, ball bearings, lens moulds, injector nozzles.

name: Tolerance 0.1 micron (interferometric)
note: Measured in wavelengths of light. Optical surfaces, diffraction gratings, semiconductor lithography much later.

name: Rough vacuum, about 1 torr (piston pump)
note: A leather-sealed piston pump. Barometry, the Magdeburg demonstration, condensers. Not enough for any electron device.

name: High vacuum, about 1e-3 torr (Sprengel mercury drop)
note: THE cheap shortcut. Falling mercury drops each trap a slug of gas and carry it out. No pistons, no seals, no tolerances. Incandescent lamps and discharge tubes live here.

name: Very high vacuum, 1e-6 torr (diffusion pump plus getters)
note: Needs a motor for the backing pump. Vacuum tubes, X-ray tubes, evaporated coatings.

name: Ultra high vacuum, 1e-9 torr (bakeable metal systems)
note: Metal gaskets, bakeout, ion pumps. Surface science and semiconductor processing.

name: Purity 99% (careful classical refining)
note: Cupellation, fire refining, recrystallisation. Rome nearly reaches this for silver and gold already.

name: Purity 99.99% (electrorefining, fractional crystallisation)
note: You cannot claim a purity you cannot measure, so this rung is gated on quantitative analysis as much as on process.

name: Purity 99.9999% (fractional distillation of volatile compounds)
note: Purify the COMPOUND, not the element. Germanium tetrachloride boils at 86 C and fractionates like brandy; germanium metal does not.

name: Purity 1 part in 1e9 (zone refining)
note: No chemistry reaches here. A travelling molten zone sweeps impurities to one end because most are more soluble in liquid than in solid. This one trick is what makes semiconductors possible at all.

name: Muscle and animal power
note: ROME HAS THIS. A man sustains roughly 75 W; an ox perhaps 400 W. Free, and the reason Roman industry is shaped the way it is.

name: Water power, tens of kW on one shaft
note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS and barely uses it for anything but grinding grain. Barbegal runs 16 overshot wheels. The technology gap is imagination, not engineering.

name: Steam power, portable, hundreds of kW
note: Power where there is no river. Until you need that, water is cheaper and needs a far shorter prerequisite chain.

name: Local electric power, kW scale
note: One dynamo on the millpond shaft you already built. Enough for arc lights, electroplating, a laboratory.

name: Grid electric power, MW scale
note: The precondition for every energy-intensive process: arc furnaces, electrolysis, aluminium, and the sustained laboratory power a purity programme eats.

name: Reproducible length standard
note: Master bars in bronze, in triplicate, in three cities. Without this nothing you write down survives you.

name: Mass to 1 milligram
note: Agate knife edges. The instrument that turns alchemy into chemistry.

name: Temperature to a few degrees (liquid in glass)
note: Fixed points at melting ice and boiling water. Without a repeatable scale no thermal recipe can be transmitted to anyone not standing beside you.

name: High temperature (clay contraction and colour pyrometry)
note: Wedgwood-style contraction pyrometer plus a calibrated colour scale. You cannot control a furnace whose temperature you cannot read.

name: Time to the second (pendulum)
note: Navigation, physics, and later every electrical measurement.

name: Time to the millisecond (chronograph, tuning fork)
note: Ballistics, engine indicating, telegraphy.

name: Absolute electrical units
note: A coil of known geometry and the Earth's field give absolute current with no calibrated instrument to start from. This is how the electrical metrology bootstrap escapes its own circularity.

name: Interferometric length (wavelengths of light)
note: Length measured against a physical constant instead of a bar of metal.

name: Oxygen and hydrogen in quantity
note: Gate on the oxy-hydrogen flame, fused quartz, balloons, and the hydrogen reduction of germanium oxide.
